specification.problem: Ideal Grover search over N=16 items on 4 qubits with one hidden marked basis state w, using one black-box phase-oracle query per iteration, 3 iterations, and readout of w from measurement counts.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Ideal (noise-free, coupling-free) 4-qubit Grover search with H, X, and multi-controlled Z diffusion. The nuclear-spin-chain physics (Rabi-driven pulses, nearest and next-nearest Ising couplings, 2πk pulse-timing condition, fidelity vs Rabi frequency) is outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: hidden marked item, as a 4-bit integer
uniform superposition over all basis states
black-box phase oracle, one query per use
fidelity with the marked state after k iterations

equations.label: Oracle and diffusion
equations.latex: O_w=I-2|w\rangle\langle w|,\qquad D=2|s\rangle\langle s|-I=H^{\otimes4}X^{\otimes4}\,(\mathrm{MCZ})\,X^{\otimes4}H^{\otimes4}\ \text{up to global phase}
equations.description: Phase flip on the marked state, and inversion about the mean. MCZ is a Z on the 4-qubit all-ones state, built as H on the target, a 3-control mcx, then H on the target.
equations.justification: Standard Grover construction. The abstract only names Grover search and does not state these equations.
assumptions: Oracle supplied as an opaque placeholder gate on 4 qubits
Diffusion equals 2|s><s|-I up to a global phase of -1

equations.label: Iteration count
equations.description: Number of Grover iterations for N=16.
equations.justification: Chosen as the standard near-optimal count. The abstract does not give the iteration number.

equations.label: Final state
equations.description: State after k Grover iterations starting from the uniform superposition.

equations.label: Fidelity vs iteration
equations.abstract_quote: We determine the temporal behaviour of the fidelity during the algorithm
equations.justification: The abstract says that fidelity is tracked during the algorithm. The ideal-case closed form is standard background recalled by me and is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: No Ising coupling or pulse errors

equations.label: Bit-order readout
equations.latex: w=\sum_{i=0}^{3}b_i2^i,\quad \text{key string}=b_3b_2b_1b_0,\quad b_i=\text{measurement of qubit }i\text{ stored in classical bit }i
equations.description: Qiskit little-endian readout. The answer is the most frequent key.
equations.justification: Fixes the encoding convention for the simulator readout.
assumptions: Measure qubit i into classical bit i

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubits (spins), qubit i is bit i of w; no ancillas

registers.name: c
registers.role: classical bits, c[i] receives qubit i

steps.description: Apply H to all 4 qubits to prepare the uniform superposition.

Repeat 3 times: place the black-box oracle once on qubits 0..3, then apply the diffusion operator (H^4, X^4, H on qubit 3, mcx with controls 0,1,2 and target 3, H on qubit 3, X^4, H^4). Total 3 oracle queries.
Measure qubits 0..3 into classical bits 0..3 and read the most frequent key as w.

specification.measurement: Measure all 4 qubits, qubit i into classical bit i. Expected success probability is about 0.961.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Take the most frequent counts key. Its string is b3b2b1b0 (last character is bit 0), and w is its integer value in base 2.
assumptions: Ideal Grover only, with no spin-chain physics
Standard Qiskit gates h, x, mcx are used, with no initialize or dense unitary
The oracle is an opaque placeholder gate and is not inspected
Optional rx/rz/cx decomposition for depth counting is not specified
